name: CI runner pool — PowerEdge: queued, admitted and running by repository
description: The PowerEdge (poweredge-xubuntu) self-hosted runner pool, as one page: what is QUEUED, what is RUNNING, for WHICH repository, and how long a runner took to start BROKEN INTO ITS PHASES. Panels 1-2 and 5-7 read the per-repository signals emitted by ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh; panels 3-4 read the fleet sums and stall classes emitted by ci-runner/k3s/phase2/runner-pod-lifecycle/scan-runner-pod-lifecycle.sh. Defined as code in livespec-dev-tooling ci-runner/observability/boards/ci-runner-pool.json and converged by apply-boards.sh beside it; edit the definition, never this board in the UI. livespec-mqy35a, livespec plan ci-runner-pod-lifecycle-reliability.

text_panel.content:
# PowerEdge runner pool

**Two datasets, on purpose.** The `livespec` environment is a Honeycomb *Metrics 2.0* environment, so **every** OTLP metric lands in its single `metrics` dataset and an `x-honeycomb-dataset` header is ignored there (measured 2026-08-23). Gauges are therefore told apart by metric NAME plus `host.name`, never by dataset — panels 1-4 and 7 all query `metrics`. The running-jobs table (panel 5) and the start-phase percentiles (panel 6) are **wide event** streams, and events auto-route by `service.name`, so they query the separate `ci-runner-pool` dataset.

**Start latency is reported PER PHASE.** Panels 6-7 break the runner-pod start into created→scheduled, scheduled→ready and ready→workflow-pod, with the work volume's provisioning inside the first. A single aggregate delta is **not** an acceptance signal — it is four stacked waits summed, so it indicts no component when it moves. One phase, ready→job-assigned, has no cluster timestamp and is not emitted; it sits inside the ready→workflow-pod number, which is therefore an upper bound on the ARC hook rather than the hook's own figure. The emission **samples**: a job whose runner and workflow pods both appear and vanish inside one 60 s tick is never observed, so a gap is an unobserved start and never a stall — `livespec.ci_pool.starts_observed` on panel 7 says which.

**Emitters.** Per-repository gauges and the running-job events: `ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh` (about every minute). Fleet sums and lifecycle stall classes: `ci-runner/k3s/phase2/runner-pod-lifecycle/scan-runner-pod-lifecycle.sh` (every 5 minutes). Both post to the host collector on `127.0.0.1:4319`.

**This board is code.** Its definition lives at `ci-runner/observability/boards/ci-runner-pool.json` in `thewoolleyman/livespec-dev-tooling` and is converged by `apply-boards.sh` beside it. A change made in this UI is lost on the next apply.

annotation.name: Pool queue depth by repository — pending and admitted workloads
annotation.description: MAX of livespec.ci_pool.queue_pending and livespec.ci_pool.queue_admitted on poweredge-xubuntu, broken down by ci.repository: one ClusterQueue datapoint per repository per tick. This is the question the fleet sums cannot answer — a saturated pool and one saturated repository look identical in livespec.ci_kueue.pending. Emitter: ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh.

annotation.name: Pool runners by repository and phase
annotation.description: MAX of livespec.ci_pool.runners on poweredge-xubuntu, broken down by ci.repository and ci.runner_phase: EphemeralRunner objects across all namespaces, counted by owning repository and phase. A repository whose runners sit in a non-Running phase is the per-repository half of a pool-wide stall. Emitter: ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh.

annotation.name: Pool fleet totals — pending and admitted against churn-slot quota and allocatable
annotation.description: MAX of the lifecycle sweep's four fleet readings on poweredge-xubuntu, ungrouped: livespec.ci_kueue.pending and .admitted against livespec.ci_churn_slot.quota_sum (the nominalQuota summed over every ClusterQueue covering ci-runner.io/churn-slot) and .allocatable (the extended resource summed over the nodes; a 0 means the resource is not registered, which IS a reading). admitted at quota with pending above zero is the pool at capacity; allocatable below quota_sum is capacity the queues believe in but the nodes do not offer. Emitter: ci-runner/k3s/phase2/runner-pod-lifecycle/scan-runner-pod-lifecycle.sh.

annotation.name: Runner-pod lifecycle stall classes — all ten
annotation.description: MAX of every livespec.ci_lifecycle.<class> gauge on poweredge-xubuntu. The sweep emits ten classes, not the seven the phase2 README's table row still names: the original pvc-pending, bind-deadline, inotify-emfile, containerd-deadline, hook-failure, stale-listener and capacity-absent, plus warm-cache-oversize, start-seed-cost and api-unavailable added since. Every class is emitted every sweep, 0 when clean, so a flat zero line is a working emitter and a MISSING line is a broken one. Emitter: ci-runner/k3s/phase2/runner-pod-lifecycle/scan-runner-pod-lifecycle.sh.

annotation.name: Pool running jobs now — repository, workflow, run id, job name, phase and age
annotation.description: The wide-event half of the pool signal: one record per runner carrying a job assignment, per tick, in the ci-runner-pool EVENTS dataset (events auto-route by service.name, so this panel does NOT read the metrics dataset the other four read). Broken down by runner and job identity over the trailing 10 minutes — about ten ticks of a roughly one-minute emitter — so a row present here is a job running now; MAX(ci.runner_age_s) is that runner's age at its newest tick and orders the table oldest first, which is where a wedged runner surfaces. Run id and job name are unbounded identifiers and are carried as event fields for exactly that reason; as gauge attributes they would multiply this pool's time series by every workflow run it ever serves. Emitter: ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh.

annotation.name: Runner start latency, BROKEN INTO PHASES — P95 per phase
annotation.description: P95 of each phase of the runner-pod start, from the start wide events (ci.record_kind = start) in the ci-runner-pool EVENTS dataset, where a percentile is exact. Read the phases, never their sum: phase 1 (created -> scheduled) indicts Kueue admission, the scheduler bind and the WaitForFirstConsumer volume provisioning, whose own sub-interval is ci.start_pvc_bound_s inside it; phase 2 (scheduled -> ready) indicts containerd's sandbox, the image and the runner process. ci.start_ready_to_workflow_pod_s is phases 3 AND 4 together and is an UPPER BOUND on the ARC container hook's prepare-job, never the hook's own number — no cluster object timestamps the job assignment that would separate them, so this emitter does not pretend to; a claim about the hook cites the hook's own log. ci.start_created_to_workflow_pod_s rides the same events as the aggregate these phases replace and is NOT charted here: it is the number that could not be acted on. Emitter: ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh.

annotation.name: Runner start phases by repository — worst start per tick, with starts observed
annotation.description: The metrics-dataset half of the same signal, and the named reader that keeps these four gauges from being indistinguishable from an emitter that stopped. MAX of livespec.ci_pool.start_created_to_scheduled_s, .start_scheduled_to_ready_s, .start_ready_to_workflow_pod_s and .start_pvc_bound_s on poweredge-xubuntu, broken down by ci.repository: each tick's datapoint is the WORST start that tick observed for that repository, because a gauge cannot carry a distribution and the slow start is the one that indicts a component. livespec.ci_pool.starts_observed rides the same panel for one reason: this emission SAMPLES starts — a job whose runner pod and workflow pod both appear and vanish inside one 60 s tick is never observed — so a gap in the four phase series means no start was seen, NOT that starts stalled, and starts_observed is emitted every tick, 0 included, to say which. Emitter: ci-runner/observability/ci-pool-attributed-gauges.sh.
